newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - LED DOWN BY TREASURIES.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - LED DOWN BY TREASURIES.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices fell 1/2 to 3/4 of a point in thin, early trade on Friday, as Treasury bonds for the second day in a row fell sharply due to concerns about this week's auctions and bearish factors.
"We're down an 0.5 from yesterday on the bid side, I don't know, I don't have buyers sticking their heads up, but it's too early on Friday," a trader said.

While Treasury bonds firmed briefly after Thursday's sale of $10 billion of 30-year bonds, because the results were seen as satisfactory, profit-taking and a weaker dollar then pushed the bonds lower, a move that continued Friday.
September Treasury bond futures pierced a few technical support levels, hitting their lowest level since July 15.
"I'd like to see it go a little lower, create some value," another trader said.
He added the recent drop in prices, which has strengthened yields, has forced some issuers to put refundings back on the shelf because they no longer stand to save enough money.
The fall in the supply of new municipal bonds should help them stabilize but in the short-term, they appeared captive to the Treasury market.
"Anytime the government market is in disarray, municipals have a difficult time because it freezes customers," a trader said.
However, the spread between the September municipal and Treasury futures this week has risen approximately 20 ticks because municipal bonds have not fallen quite as steeply as Treasuries.

With New York City Water Finance Authority's new $288 million of bonds freed to trade on Thursday, and expectations that Pittsburgh Airport will take the same action on Friday with its $453 million of revenue bonds, traders said the market in newly issued bonds might be fairly active.
Standard and Poor's Corp's Blue List was little changed at just over $1.4 billion. The yardstick measures the value of existing bonds offered for sale.

September municipal bond futures fell 21 ticks to 119-17/32, while September Treasury bond futures slid 28 ticks to 113-11/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 198 ticks, a seven-tick gain from Thursday's close.
In the secondary market, Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority of 2024, which pay a 5.0 percent coupon, were bid at 5.52 percent, NET, down four basis points.
And Jefferson County, Alabama, Sewer Revenues of 2027, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were offered at 99, down 1/2 a point.
